A_target.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be the [[Definition:Substitution (Combinatorics on Words)|substitution]] $0 \mapsto 01$, $1 \mapsto 10$.
Then the [[Definition:Thue-Morse Sequence|Thue-Morse word]] $t$ is the [[Definition:Unique|unique]] infinite word beginning with $0$ such that:
:$\map \sigma t = t$

B_source.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a substitution [[Definition:Prolongable Substitution|prolongable]] at a letter $a$, that is, $\map \sigma a = a u$ with $u$ non-empty.
Then the iterates $\map {\sigma^n} a$ converge in the [[Definition:Product Topology|product topology]] to an infinite word.

substitutions.the prolongable substitution: the map sending zero to zero-one and one to one-zero
substitutions.the iterates from a single letter: successive images of the letter zero, each extending the previous

derived.the limit is unchanged by the substituti: the word is a fixed point of the substitution
derived.each iterate being a prefix of the next: convergence letterwise, so the limit is well defined

object_map.reformulation: Present the infinite word as what iterating the substitution converges to, making it a fixed point of that map.

validity_conditions: The substitution is prolongable at zero, meaning the image of zero begins with zero, so each iterate is a prefix of the next.
The iterates therefore agree on longer and longer prefixes, so they converge letterwise and the limit is a well-defined infinite word.
Continuity of the substitution on infinite words carries the fixed point property to the limit; uniqueness follows since the first letter determines the whole word by iteration.
proof_plan: $\map \sigma 0 = 0 1$ begins with $0$, so $\sigma$ is prolongable at $0$.

Iterating from $0$:
:$0, \, 01, \, 0110, \, 01101001, \ldots$
Each iterate is a prefix of the next, as $\map {\sigma^{n + 1} } 0 = \map {\sigma^n} {01} = \map {\sigma^n} 0 \map {\sigma^n} 1$.
The letterwise limit is an infinite word $t$ whose prefix of length $2^n$ is $\map {\sigma^n} 0$.

$\sigma$ is continuous in the product topology.
Hence $\map \sigma t = \lim \map {\sigma^{n + 1} } 0 = t$.
Any fixed point beginning with $0$ has $\map {\sigma^n} 0$ as a prefix for all $n$, so equals $t$.
{{qed}}
